frames.title: Use light to shape mood and hierarchy
frames.summary: Lighting defines what the audience feels first, what they notice second, and what remains uncertain.
principles: Control direction, contrast, and softness to shape emotional reading.
Motivation should feel coherent even when stylized.
Key-to-fill balance signals openness, mystery, or threat.
Let practical sources support story geography and performance focus.
patterns: Use backlight and separation when identity or isolation matters.
Shift lighting logic across a sequence as the power dynamic changes.
antiPatterns: Do not light everything evenly unless neutrality is the point.
Do not let beautiful light contradict the scene's dramatic need.

frames.title: Build a color system with emotional logic
frames.summary: Color becomes meaningful when palettes repeat with narrative intention instead of random taste.
principles: Define what each palette family communicates in this project.
Use contrast in hue, value, or saturation to spotlight emotional change.
Let costume, production design, and light collaborate rather than compete.
Save major palette shifts for turning points or new realities.
patterns: Associate a character or faction with a limited palette range before evolving it.
Use desaturation or contamination when safety or certainty is collapsing.
antiPatterns: Do not rely on generic color symbolism without project-specific meaning.
Do not over-code every frame until nuance disappears.
